source.title: Interpretability Without Tradeoffs: Disentangling Polysemanticity At Equal Predictive Performance
source.authors: Dogukan Bagci; B. Schiele; Simone Schaub-Meyer; Jonas Fischer; Robin Hesse

page_placements.theme: Polysemantic neurons can be split into more monosemantic components (upstream inputs, weights, downstream paths)

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines mixed visual-unit activations and whether disentanglement produces more coherent units, using a new method and measures rather than reproducing the original neuron example.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative top-activating-image examples for individual DINOv2 units and quantitative interpretability and classification results for ELUDe. Its steering captions are induced interventions, so they are not evidence about naturally occurring polysemanticity. References to prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a method paper (ELUDe, a lossless post-hoc split of units into subunits). Its only own result bearing on a claim version is V1. It shows top-activating ImageNet images for individual DINOv2-B/14 last-layer units that mix unrelated concepts (artichokes, sand, bookshelves; rotary phones, beaches, graduation). That is a new setting, a self-supervised ViT rather than InceptionV1. The evidence is qualitative, from a few hand-picked units with hand-assigned labels. The quantitative tables measure the method's interpretability and faithfulness against SAE baselines, not polysemanticity in the model.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that ELUDe splits polysemantic units into more monosemantic subunits that sum exactly to the original, so outputs are unchanged by construction. They report that it reaches state-of-the-art or competitive interpretability against SAEs and transcoders, with higher stability, low memory cost and qualitative steering ability. They frame this as 'interpretability without a tradeoff'.
record.recipe_differences: Uses top-activating image instances, upstream contribution clustering, and weight restructuring with ELUDe; it does not reproduce the original neuron-specific method or examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper notes that the probing dataset and top-k choice determine which concepts can be extracted; larger k may include a broader range of activation strengths and concepts. It also reports qualitative robustness across selected clustering hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-hoc rewiring splits each original unit into subunits whose summed output is exactly the original. The subunits score higher on coherence (MS-Score about 36 to 71 on DINOv2-B/14; VLM-judge rank 8 to 1), and accuracy is unchanged across ViTs, SigLIP2 and ConvNeXtV2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemantic vision units can be decomposed losslessly into more coherent subunits, with no change to model outputs.

record.problems: The neuron examples are qualitative and a small illustrative selection, with visible-theme labels assigned by hand. The interpretability metrics are based on top-activating images and include VLM judges; the paper does not quantify how prevalent polysemantic units are or establish that the displayed themes lack any broader shared feature. It reports no quantitative language-model evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: The paper's steering examples are purpose-induced caption changes, not measurements of naturally occurring polysemanticity. Stability and computational-efficiency results concern method properties rather than the claim versions. No other claim-relevant results were omitted.

untested.parts: InceptionV1 and the cat-face/car-front example are not examined. No prevalence estimate: units are hand-selected illustrations with hand labels.
No language-model MLP neurons are measured. LLaVA is used only for induced steering on the vision encoder.
Superposition is cited as the usual explanation; it is not tested.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures or regularization on the share of polysemantic neurons. Post-hoc ELUDe splitting is not a change to architecture or training.
There is no systematic test of whether mixed units share a higher-level feature. Several examples mix related categories (spiders/insects, reptiles & arthropods, several dog groups).
Top-k choice is noted to affect which concepts appear (larger k gives a broader activation range), but this is not varied as a test of whether a unit counts as polysemantic.

missing.what: Coherence of the original backbone's units as judged by VLMs: the backbone-only consensus win rate is 38.74% on DINOv2 and 45.44% on ViT-B/16, below most decomposition methods. This is a weak quantitative indicator that original units are less coherent; useful context for V1-like claims in ViTs.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked R9–R18 to V5, which is wrong. V5 concerns how architecture or training choices change the model's own polysemanticity. ELUDe is a post-hoc analysis tool, and those rows compare the method with baselines. Effective expansion factors of about 8 clusters per neuron (Table 9) are tuned through min_cluster_size and TopK to match the SAE expansion factors, so they are not a prevalence measure of polysemanticity. The steering results are induced interventions and were rightly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 or the specific cat-face, car-front and cat-leg example.
No quantitative evaluation of language-model MLP neurons; the LLaVA result is qualitative vision-side steering, not a test of polysemanticity prevalence.
Superposition and capacity pressure are discussed as a possible attribution, but are not experimentally tested.
Initialization, regularization, and training-noise causes under adequate capacity are not tested.

The study tests whether ELUDe can improve measured interpretability while retaining image-classification accuracy in several vision models. It does not compare activation functions or regularization choices, nor measure the fraction of polysemantic neurons across those choices.

The illustrative examples show groups of visually different top-activating images, but the study does not systematically test whether such groups share a higher-level feature or are truly unrelated, or estimate how often either interpretation applies.
The study defines scores using top-activating images but does not systematically vary the activation range or explanation-scoring method to test measurement dependence.

relation.reason: The figures are the study's own results and bear on whether V1 holds in DINOv2. They are qualitative and selected, but the claim is about existence.

tranche.reason: V1 is an existence claim. The paper shows its own top-activating ImageNet images for DINOv2-B/14 last-layer units that the authors call polysemantic, mixing unrelated concepts (Figs 1, 3, 12-17). That is a result on V1 in a new setting (self-supervised ViT), not only method performance.

source_check.notes: V1 evidence is qualitative: 7 author-selected DINOv2-B/14 layer-12 units, hand-labelled subunits, no prevalence. The controls and uncertainty flags apply only to the method benchmarks. The paper is inconsistent: DINOv2-B/14 backbone MS-Score/accuracy is 36.42/85.1 in Table 2 but 36.2/84.3 in Table 6 (R11, R12, R17, R18). ELUDe's effective EF is 11.41 in the 'EF16' setting and 5.91 at layer 11 (Table 9).

statements.problem: Concept names are hand-assigned labels of ELUDe subunits. Those subunits are clusters of the parent's top-k activation instances, so 'parent units' top images mix' is a fair reading. The statement already says the units were selected/hand-picked.

statements.correction: Neuron 31 subunit labels: Artichokes, Dogs, Dogs, Fur coats, Marine animals, Sand, Bookshelves, Dogs on bed.
statements.problem: Says nothing about this study; the cited R1 refers to another study. For this study, R1 labels overlap (Dogs x3, Fur coats).

Accurately paraphrases the authors' design statement (Sec 3.1): the probing dataset defines extractable concepts, and higher k may capture more concepts. It is not a measured sensitivity, and the statement does not claim one.

statements.correction: DINOv2-B/14 MS-Score 36.42 to 71.05; LLM rank 8 to 1; accuracy 85.1 to 85.10; R2 100.
